title: Prove two fixed-observation P104 repair obstructions on #7830
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

- **Rational chart 282.** After the funded retargets and withdrawal of slots 88960 and 90369, the retained arrivals have rank three. Adding the five protected reader rows raises the rank to five. One replacement scalar cannot supply the two missing directions, even with an arbitrary payload.
- **Binary adjoint charts 510–518.** Of 90 grade-one sender-pair choices, 27 span the two required directions if all stock is granted regardless of time. Every such choice requires a protected reader that depends on the send itself. Even granting the cheapest higher-grade replacements at all nine banks leaves at least 2.10634752732049428 signed binary units short at κ = 0.003889928046155.

The results fix the other paid payloads, productive credit and caller boundaries specified in the packages. They close the stated repair routes with zero κ credit.

## Task and overlap

This is a scoped follow-up to #7830 at `14c74c6a67108f675ac1196a5f2415ead0920e71`, based on upstream main `e54523517d0f03e58352e647c403a5af3e525a57`. It takes the funded observation in #7795 through the downstream reader test and gives a causal closure check for the nine binary receivers on the retained #7786 word. The supporting receipts record the separate #7793, #7804 and #7776 questions with their own scopes. [Investigation thread](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/7111)

## Validation

Both Python 3 standard-library replays reproduced the frozen result bytes from commit-pinned inputs in about 1–2 seconds each. The rational controls detect a perturbed outlet coefficient and omitted ingress sends. The binary replay checks all 462,400 operator coefficients and all 3,554 dirty retirements per orientation, the caller and the signed invoice. Its controls reject a missing retirement and detect omission of the owner-411 feed. Each package gives the exact commands and input hashes. [Rational replay](https://github.com/Clear1nsight/integer-mult-bounds/blob/d83f58fb7bf4bc8d6005de67218e6bcbd62d9a8c/research/p104-chart282-reader-cut/README.md#reproduction) · [Binary replay](https://github.com/Clear1nsight/integer-mult-bounds/blob/d83f58fb7bf4bc8d6005de67218e6bcbd62d9a8c/research/p104-binary-three-ingress-cut/README.md#reproduction)

## Credit

Credit the #7786 and #7830 constructions, Ali Romman’s paired BIT caller and #7776 supplier, and the authors of the linked questions. Clear1nsight prepared the package with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance, including separate computational reviews.

## Open next questions

At chart 282, allow both funded arrivals 88959 and 88960 to change while rerouting 90369. Test the reader rank at the actual clocks modulo the surviving arrivals 90605 and 90604. More than two missing directions closes that instance. If the rank permits two, check causal sources for both payloads and restore side reader 89187 before pricing the actual edit. For the binary cut, changing one protected egress first requires its downstream demand and replacement costs to be accounted for. Independent human review of both scoped arguments is welcome.
